newsitem.title: USA: Bethlehem Steel operating at high levels-CEO.
newsitem.headline: Bethlehem Steel operating at high levels-CEO.

text.p: Bethlehem Steel Corp expects to operate at high levels of capacity this year, chief executive Curtis Barnette said Wednesday.
"We expect to operate at very high levels thoughout the year," he told the company's quarterly media teleconference.
However, a spokesman later declined to say at what capacity the company's plants are now operating.
Stating "steel demand continues to be good," Barnette said the company now has an order "backlog of about three months."

Earlier Wednesday, the second largest U.S. steel company reported second quarter earnings before a gain of $1.01 on the sale of its Iron Ore Co of Canada stake were $0.32 per share -- well above First Call's consensus estimate of $0.23.

During the teleconference, Barnette declined to comment on analysts' estimates for the rest of the year -- $0.19 and $0.17 per share for the third and fourth quarters, respectively -- saying, "We do not forecast results."
Noting the company's efforts to pay down its unfunded pension liabilities, he said completion of this will reduce the company's annual pension expense $110 million.
This would increase pretax profits by a like amount, he noted. Second quarter pretax profits were $192.0 million.
By June 30, the company said, the pension liability had been reduced to $685 million from $1.6 billion at the end of 1993.
Barnette said application of year-end adjustments to reflect stock market changes would cut the pension liability another $150 million.
He said Bethlehem Steel's Sparrows Point Division will have complete plans on the facility's previously discussed cold rolled mill mondernization "in the near future."
He declined to say what he meant by "the near future," but said the proposal is now undergoing enginering review.
Barnette said no decision has been made on whether to put the new cold rolled mill at Sparrows Point, the company's steel mill near Baltimore, or at an offsite location.
He said talks continue on the sale of BethForge, CENTEC and BethShip, decling to be more specific.
